A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraphOmni and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and extensive appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine LLMs on six graph tasks, alongside RL-Opt and RL-Scale experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds o4-mini evaluations, partial Qwen3-8B results, and additional model-response cases.

M1.justification: Appendix C.1 revises the specified RL policy and Q-network inputs from individual graph instance s to task-and-difficulty state s0. This is a localized change in the method specification; DQN, sequential factor selection, MLP architecture, and MSE loss remain. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed accordingly.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same six tasks, seven synthetic graph families, seven serialization formats, nine prompt schemes, and benchmark of 241,726 queries. The new models use retained task coverage; real-world, temporal, and noisy-graph evaluations are proposed only as future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds o4-mini to the main LLM comparison and Qwen3-8B to the partial comparison in Appendix D.6. All nine earlier LLMs, task-specific random baselines, and the RL-versus-grid-search comparison are retained.

E3.justification: The added Qwen3-8B evaluation uses a random subset of existing queries. Appendix A.1 specifies 25%, whereas D.6 specifies approximately 20%, leaving the exact fraction unresolved. Existing difficulty definitions, five-shot settings, accuracy criteria, and stated RL training budgets remain.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a Qwen3 diameter-error case involving overlooked shorter paths and an o4-mini triangle-counting error involving incorrect connectivity. Appendix D.4 adds further response traces. Earlier error cases and the principal sensitivity and scalability analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean accuracy with 95% confidence intervals across factor combinations and standard errors for token-usage plots. No new repeated-run, seed, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation practice is documented. Changed interval margins are result changes.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands results with o4-mini across all tasks and partial Qwen3 results, including 93.06% hard-cycle accuracy for o4-mini and 61.97% easy-BFS accuracy for Qwen3. The original nine models' Table 3 values remain unchanged. Several appendix aggregate means and confidence-interval margins change, including margins for unchanged open-model means. v1's Table 7 of RL-Scale top-eight configurations and accuracies is removed, while RL-Opt Table 4 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 revises the policy domain, expected-reward objective, and Bellman terminal condition to condition on task/difficulty s0 and average over graph instances and LLM responses. This changes the formal conditioning, beyond notation alone. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace GPT-4o with o4-mini alongside Claude-3.5 as the highlighted leading models and emphasize economical RL search. The central contributions—comprehensive benchmarking, modular evaluation, configuration sensitivity, and adaptive factor selection—retain their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix F explicitly discusses limits from synthetic graphs, canonical tasks, and controlled environments. v2 interprets reasoning-model results as narrowing some capability gaps while difficult global tasks remain challenging. Section 4.3 corrects the RL cost interpretation from a 25% reduction to roughly 25% of exhaustive-search cost, although Appendix C.2 retains the earlier wording.

D1.justification: v2 adds project-specific code and dataset access links, identifiers for the added models, and Algorithm 1 documenting RL initialization, action selection, and updates. Exploration decay remains ambiguously documented: the prose specifies linear decay, while the pseudocode multiplies by a decay rate.

R1.justification: The introduction adds background citations on foundational LLMs, GNN applications, and benchmarks such as MMLU, MMLU-Pro, and MATH. The graph-benchmark comparison and claimed research gap remain substantially unchanged. Publication updates and consolidation of duplicate references do not introduce different cited research.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract, edits author/header text and explanatory prose, moves the main related-work discussion into Appendix E, and relocates two existing findings to D.5. Task-specific D.2 subsections improve navigation. These are targeted revisions within a largely retained narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds the pipeline diagram in Figure 3 and the Qwen3 comparison in Figure 27/Table 16. Existing radar charts, Table 3, and appendix heatmaps gain o4-mini entries, with revised captions and ranking highlights. Algorithm 1 is added and the RL-Scale configuration table is removed; most existing display designs remain.

improvement.justification: The added reasoning-model evaluations test whether earlier capability limitations persist, while resource links, explicit RL pseudocode, and applicability limitations improve usability and interpretation. These provide a limited overall gain. Conflicting Qwen3 sample fractions, inconsistent RL descriptions, and removal of the detailed RL-Scale results table weaken the revision's clarity and prevent a stronger assessment.
